problem:
Lagrange's method can be used to reduce the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{3}$ to the canonical form given below. 

$$
{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-2{y}_{3}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=\boxed{} \\ {y}_{2}=\boxed{} \\ {y}_{3}={x}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom, what is missing from the blank spaces?

feedback.problem:
Lagrange's method can be used to reduce the quadratic form $Q(x)=4{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}$ to the canonical form given below. 

$$
\boxed{}\,{y}_{1}^{2}-5{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=\boxed{} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what is missing from the blank spaces?
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply Lagrange's method as follows:

First, we group ${x}_{1}^{2}$-term with all cross-product terms that contain ${x}_{1}$ and factor out the coefficient of ${x}_{1}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(4{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =4({x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}4({x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} & =4([{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}]-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =4(({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2})-{x}_{2}^{2} & =4({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =4({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the canonical form is

$$
4{y}_{1}^{2}-5{y}_{2}^{2},\,{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}={x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the missing parts are as follows:

$\,$ $4\,$ and $\,{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}.$
